name: consent capture, gating, and lifecycle enforcement
definition: Affirmative choice, granular categories, withdrawal, runtime/state propagation, pre-consent blocking, and honoring recorded consent across components, iframes, SDKs, and permissions.

name: consent recordkeeping and audit trail
definition: Evidence and accountability for consent: storing exact wording, timestamp, version, identity/IP, withdrawal logs, audit trails, or disputing whether a checkbox alone suffices.

name: consent control defeated by timing, persistence, or removal
definition: A privacy control is undermined because collection occurs before the user can act, a setting does not survive restart, a widget fails, or exit controls are removed, distorted, or mandatory.

name: privacy notice and consent interface defects
definition: Presence, legibility, wording, dismissal, locale, accessibility, or geo-scoping of privacy notices and consent banners at collection, including misleading opt-out instructions and a link substituted for a working mechanism.

name: default-on collection and opt-in/opt-out model
definition: Data practices active unless the user opts out, or debate over opt-in versus opt-out models, covering analytics, telemetry, upload, or persistence enabled by default without an affirmative act.

name: notice presence, reachability, accuracy, and maintenance
definition: Whether a privacy notice, policy page, or transparency document exists, is reachable, correctly linked, and accurately reflects practice, including editing, translating, recovering redirects, or documenting configuration.

name: transparency, purpose disclosure, and documented trust assumptions
definition: Remedy is to explain purposes, permissions, retention, or residual risk more clearly, or document and warn users about a trust assumption, rather than change the underlying practice.

name: jurisdiction scope, cross-border transfer, and legal-authority compliance
definition: Geography or named law scopes a notice or data flow (EU vs non-EU, CCPA/GDPR, IP-as-PII by region) or the request, refusal, or deferral rests on external legal duty, regulator, DPO, or compliance assertion.

name: data inventory, retention, purpose limitation, and minimization
definition: Enumerates personal data stored or logged and specifies retention, expiry, overruns, or purpose; includes debate over whether data is processed at all (transient vs stored) versus unbounded retention, and field-level minimization.

name: right-to-erasure requests, deletion scope, and portability
definition: Data-subject requests for deletion, right-to-be-forgotten, export/portability, or rights scoping, including no self-service path, admin stop-gaps, over-broad clear/delete actions, and conflicts with audit trails, legal hold, shared organizations, or downstream packages.

name: erasure semantics, tooling failure, and residual stores
definition: Disputes whether a privacy operation deletes or anonymizes records, conflicts erasure with mandated retention, or documents an eraser aborting on config/schema errors or leaving PII in logs and secondary stores.

name: anonymization technique, coverage, re-identification, and media redaction
definition: Masking, hashing, truncation, redaction, substitution, or blurring; reports identifiers surviving in headers, free text, logs, or export boundaries; or documents pseudonymization reversible, linkable, recomputable, or defeated at a role boundary.

name: location precision, spatial generalization, encryption, and aggregation safeguards
definition: Reducing location granularity so it cannot pinpoint a person (coordinate precision, geoblocks, snapping, adaptive radii) or technical safeguards so released data cannot decrypt or re-identify: key destruction, decryption thresholds, minimum cohort counts.

name: third-party analytics, embeds, and processor exposure
definition: Named external analytics, trackers, CDNs, relays, ads, fonts, webhooks, or bundled tracker SDKs receive or can access personal data, with anonymization, pre-hashing, proxying, opt-out, removal, or stripped builds framed as remedy, including transfer without consent.

name: data minimization, local-first processing, and configuration suppression
definition: Collect, request, or retain less personal data, keep data local or on-device unless explicitly sent, or argue a rule does not apply because a service is configured to suppress cookies, fingerprints, or IPs.

name: credential, secret exposure, and cryptographic/key protection
definition: Secret material (keys, tokens, share secrets, passwords) appears in an unintended channel such as public repo, analytics dashboard, P2P share, or observability store, or is stored unencrypted/verbatim; includes weak password storage and key-management redesign requests.

name: access control integrity, field visibility, and tenant scoping
definition: Limiting who can view or operate on personal data via roles, per-field/record visibility, identity-binding proof, tenant filters, and admin operations, and failures where settings, tabs, unguessable URLs, or secret links substitute for real access control or desynchronize.

name: user control over stored state, telemetry settings, and analytics opt-out
definition: User-facing control over stored state or data egress: deleting cookies/local data, disabling remote pushes, in-memory store choice, discovering telemetry settings, opting out of analytics, or optional/configurable invasive features, plus DNT signaling.

name: logging, output, and harvested identifiers as disclosure channel
definition: Diagnostic logs, error messages, generated output, or automatically harvested metadata (git-log contacts, POM emails, contributor lists) are unintended channels for sensitive data, with masking, redaction, immutable-history caveats, or log expiry proposed.

name: telemetry payload exposure, server-log access, and retention
definition: What server/platform logs, telemetry payloads, diagnostics, stack traces, breadcrumbs, or debug details collect; who can access them; how long they are kept; PII content; public debug disclosure; and missing redaction hooks.

name: sensitive-context amplification, vulnerable groups, and public-interest tradeoff
definition: Privacy harm amplified by sensitive domain or vulnerable population (minors, Tor/marginalized users, harassment targets), sector-specific sensitive data such as financial or legal records, or explicit balancing against public health, funder reporting, or functionality.

name: privacy versus product, security, or platform constraint tradeoff
definition: Reasoned opposition to a privacy request because the practice serves security, anti-abuse, or core product function, granular controls complicate API consistency, or OS/browser/upstream requirements make it unavoidable (including custom crypto instead of standards).

name: execution of untrusted code and cross-site session exposure
definition: External or user-supplied scripts run in a page context with access to credentials, cookies, or DOM data, or an injection flaw renders untrusted data unescaped, allowing script execution that reads session tokens.

name: responsibility boundary, policy ownership, and dismissal/deferral
definition: Raises where a privacy obligation or policy decision should sit (library vs downstream developer, instance admin, DB layer, standards body), or dismisses/postpones a concern as false positive, expected behavior, another issue, plugin, vendor, or user responsibility without substantive investigation.

name: closure quality, stale/deferred status, and scanner or unreproducible disputes
definition: Resolution quality is contested: closure by roadmap promise, stale-bot, wontfix, duplicate redirect, private unverified outcome, vague report, or contested scanner evidence without diff, test, or reporter confirmation; also shipped fixes disputed as incomplete, and lifecycle metadata like severity/priority conflicts.

name: consent implementation tradeoffs, deadline pressure, and monetization
definition: Tradeoffs prioritizing visual parity, MVP scope, Storybook-only integration, performance, or a statutory date over completing the privacy mechanism, or delivering compliance as a separately priced add-on.

name: restricted data redistribution, license-driven design, and remote uninstall purge
definition: An externally imposed license, EULA, or distribution restriction on a data source forces redesign of how data is obtained, consented to, or refreshed, or app/account removal hides rather than deletes stored data requiring a lifecycle purge hook.

name: evidence: complete body and discussion
definition: The artifact carries a current-snapshot issue body and all retrievable comments, so proposal, discussion and any recorded outcome can be assessed directly.

name: evidence: partial snapshot
definition: Some body or discussion text is retrievable but comments, attachments or edited content are known to be missing, so conclusions about discussion or outcome are limited.

name: evidence: metadata only
definition: Only released metadata (title, labels, counts, dates, matched keywords) is available; no body or comment text can be read.

name: evidence: title or keyword only, content unreadable
definition: A title or matched keyword is the only semantic signal, and even metadata-level context is insufficient to support a concrete privacy mechanism.
